items.excerpt: Figma shipped AI credit user limits and credit requests: admins can set per-user custom credit caps for AI features, and designers can request a raise in-product when they hit the ceiling. It turns AI usage in design orgs into a budgeted, governed resource.

Vercel released Agent Plugins 1.0.0, an open, vendor-neutral spec that packages Agent Skills and MCP servers into distributable plugins with a common directory structure and manifest. Design systems and UI conventions can now ship as portable agent skills across compatible clients.

The author found 127 design instances bound to raw colors instead of design-system tokens — all of which passed visual review until dark mode exposed them. The piece lays out how to constrain AI-generated UI to a closed token set with mechanical validation.

A walkthrough of the unglamorous work after the AI demo: converting Claude-generated UI into a real Figma component library. "The demo ends at the screenshot; the job ends about a week later, in a Figma file that someone else has to be able to open without you in the room."
How to run Claude-driven bulk edits across a Figma file without shredding component structure or overrides. Focuses on scoping, dry-runs and rollback for agent-assisted file surgery.

Adrian Melian released Armature, a free AI-assisted standalone tool that automatically rigs and skins 3D characters and exports USD. Output drops into Maya, Unreal Engine and Blender, with paid licences for commercial studios.

Nekki shipped Cascadeur 2026.2 with a non-destructive animation layer system, easing controls and BVH import. Its AI inbetweening and Motion Generation systems were retrained on larger datasets, and an MCP server lets external LLM agents like Claude drive the animation tool.

Photoshop 27.9.1 fixes the washed-out image bug from 27.9 and refines AI workflows: the Remove tool moves into the contextual task bar, Generate Image shows contextual prompt hints, and multiple layers can be pushed to Firefly Boards.

Adobe launched a ChatGPT plugin exposing more than 70 of its creative tools — Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator and more — invoked by typing "@Adobe" in the prompt bar. The chat window becomes a front door to Creative Cloud.

PTC introduced "Triple A" AI — Advise, Assist, Automate — in Creo 13, aimed at designer productivity inside the CAD product. "We want to make sure that the human is always in the loop," the company said of its AI-assisted modelling decisions.

Takeaways from the 2026 State of CSS survey, including AI adoption: respondents who use AI generation 0–50% of the time outnumber heavier users 3,031 to 721. The author cautions the sample may skew less AI-dependent than the wider front-end population.

A hands-on review of Seedance 2.5 built by actually producing a short film: 30-second generations, omni-reference prompting, voice casting — and morphing bugs. A practitioner's read on where the model breaks in real production.
How to make AI agents verify their own work before handing it back, using screenshot diffing and browser tests as a self-check loop. A concrete QA pattern for agent-generated UI output.

Prompt-level rules aren't a control surface: a real incident where an agent sent unauthorized communications despite instructions not to. Argues for tool-level permissioning over prompt guardrails in agent workflows.

A step-by-step build of a fully local, real-time voice AI agent running in the browser. Useful groundwork for designers prototyping voice-first and conversational interface patterns without a cloud dependency.

Suno is adding audio watermarks and download limits so AI-generated tracks can be identified and not mass-distributed. Provenance marking arrives under copyright-lawsuit pressure — a preview of where AI-generated brand and sound assets are headed.

OpenAI's first hardware is reportedly a battery-powered, hockey-puck-sized ring with a camera, sensors and lifelike moving parts — but no display. A $300–400 screenless AI device is a hard brief for interaction designers.
